cause_quote: The added `const running = runWithGatewayDetachedWorkContinuation(` wrapped `launchCronRun` in a scope that could drain as soon as the launch returned a cancellation result, while the untracked core-and-webhook promise was still pending.
user_saw: An operator could see an `Async work scope is closed` warning after cancelling a cron run whose cleanup was still pending.
summary: The fix registers the core-and-webhook promise with `trackAsyncWork` so delayed cleanup can finish after cancellation returns.
reasoning: The parent already supported early cancellation, and its scheduled tick ran through `runInDetachedAsyncContext`, so returning from the run did not close a per-launch async-work scope beneath cleanup. I checked that the host-launcher diff placed that same cancellation race inside a fresh scope whose owner drains when tracked work finishes. The fix's inverse test reproduced the failure when delayed cleanup tried to register work after the scope closed.
